skill.name: embedded-captions
skill.description: Creates embedded captions for single-subject talking-head videos using local transcription, subject matting, themed layouts, preview checks, and FFmpeg-based compositing.
skill.summary: Create readable or cinematic captions that integrate with a single-subject talking-head video.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most scanner alerts are false positives caused by artistic theme names, Markdown backticks, fixed path resolution, and local media tooling. Confirmed risks include silent self-update instructions, runtime third-party execution through uvx, CDN script loads, and broad process cleanup. The skill should not publish until these behaviors are removed or require explicit consent. Static review was capped at 400/1481 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 1081 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs agents to update itself silently before use.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the silent update command. Require explicit user approval before any network update or global skill modification.

remediation.issue: Transcription downloads and executes WhisperX through uvx at runtime.
remediation.suggestion: Use a preinstalled, hash-verified dependency or request consent before installation. Lock the package and its transitive dependencies.

remediation.issue: Several executable HTML files load GSAP from a CDN without integrity protection.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle GSAP locally or add verified Subresource Integrity and a restrictive Content Security Policy to every executable HTML file.

remediation.issue: Renderer timeout cleanup uses a broad pkill pattern.
remediation.suggestion: Track and terminate only child process identifiers created by the current render. Avoid pattern-based termination of unrelated Puppeteer sessions.

content.user_title: Create Embedded Captions for Talking-Head Videos
content.value_statement: Talking-head videos need readable captions that fit the speaker and scene. This skill transcribes speech, mattes the subject, previews layouts, and renders styled captions.
actual_capabilities: Transcribes speech with word timings through WhisperX, with a local Hyperframes fallback.
Creates subject mattes and background frames for behind-the-person caption effects.
Selects from 36 visual identities for readable rails or cinematic embedded typography.
Compiles caption plans into background and foreground HTML render layers.
Runs timing, occlusion, overflow, and rail handoff checks before rendering.
Composites captions, source video, matte frames, and optional plate effects into final video files.
limitations: Requires a built Hyperframes checkout plus Node.js, FFmpeg, Python, and compatible local rendering dependencies.
Supports single-subject talking-head clips; multi-shot or multi-speaker footage must be split first.
Automatic transcription and matting can fail on silence, strong accents, busy motion, props, or difficult backgrounds.
First runs may download WhisperX packages, model weights, and external browser assets.

use_cases.title: Caption Social Videos
use_cases.description: Add readable subtitles and one visual emphasis moment to short talking-head clips.

use_cases.title: Design Cinematic Typography
use_cases.description: Place selected phrases behind the speaker using subject mattes, safe zones, and timed motion.

use_cases.title: Standardize Branded Captions
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent caption identity across interviews, product updates, and executive communications.

prompt_templates.title: Add Clear Captions
prompt_templates.prompt: Add clear captions to this single-speaker talking-head video. Use the anchor identity, preserve the footage, and provide preview frames before rendering.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a readable caption rail.

prompt_templates.title: Recommend a Caption Identity
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this clip and recommend three caption identities based on tone, framing, scene brightness, and readability. Explain one preferred choice.
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose a visual direction before authoring.

prompt_templates.title: Create Cinematic Embedded Captions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create cinematic embedded captions for this interview. Promote only the strongest phrase, keep transcript timing exact, and fix every preview issue before rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Themed Caption Composition
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a themed caption composition for this product reveal. Use safe zones, validate occlusion and overflow, render both layers, then apply plate effects.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with layered rendering and scene reactions.

output_examples.input: A 20-second product update with one speaker, a bright office background, and a requirement that every word remains readable.
output: Recommended identity: anchor, because its opaque rail protects readability on the bright scene.
Preview result: one lower-third rail and one restrained embedded climax.
Delivery: a composited video with validated timing, overflow, and handoff checks.

output_examples.input: A dark interview clip requesting cinematic captions with one strong emotional phrase.
output: Recommended identity: cream, because the warm dark scene supports screen-blended typography.
Composition: grouped narration near the silhouette and one large phrase behind the subject.
Review result: adjusted placement after checking occlusion, contrast, and reading order.

output_examples.input: A high-energy product reveal requesting a themed visual effect and final plate reaction.
output: Recommended identity: ordnance for a heavy announcement style.
Render plan: foreground rail, embedded apex, subject matte, and synchronized plate punch.
Delivery: final video plus preview frames and gate results.

best_practices: Confirm the clip has one clear speaker, usable speech, and no existing burned captions.
Read safe-zone and transcript outputs before choosing placement, emphasis, and identity.
Review preview frames for contrast, reading order, overlap, clipping, and subject occlusion before rendering.
anti_patterns: Do not embed every spoken word behind the subject; keep full text on a readable rail when needed.
Do not render multi-shot or silent footage without splitting clips and validating the transcript.
Do not bypass timing, occlusion, overflow, or handoff checks to force a final render.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: No API key is required. Local tools perform transcription, matting, layout checks, rendering, and compositing.

faq.question: What video input works best?
faq.answer: Use a single-speaker talking-head clip with clear speech, a visible face, stable framing, and no burned captions.

faq.question: Can I choose a caption style?
faq.answer: Yes. The catalog includes readable rail styles, cinematic embedded styles, and themed visual-effect identities.

faq.question: Does the skill preserve the source footage?
faq.answer: Standard and cinematic workflows preserve the footage. Some themed identities add approved plate reactions after compositing.

faq.question: Can it work without network access?
faq.answer: Not completely. First runs may download packages or model weights, and several templates load GSAP from a CDN.

faq.question: Does it support multiple languages?
faq.answer: WhisperX can detect or accept a language setting. Accuracy still depends on speech clarity, accent, and model choice.
